subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw implement a safe binary-document fallback in the shared `read` tool now, or defer direct `read` behavior to broader document extraction/provider-native file work?
rationale: Source inspection proves the token-waste path still exists, but the issue proposes multiple user-visible directions and has an open conflicting implementation candidate, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Ship Safe Fallback
options.body: Add bounded detection in the current shared `read` path and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

options.title: Defer To Document Work
options.body: Keep this issue tied to broader document parsing or provider-native file support, accepting that direct `read` can still waste tokens until that lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update the tool description or prompt guidance without runtime blocking, reducing risk but not reliably preventing accidental binary reads.

recommendation.title: Ship Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add bounded detection in the current shared `read` path and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal is on the read wrapper, Office path normalization, and adjacent media input code this choice would affect.
